items.description: Sec. 4.1 gives only '40×20×8 elements'. It doesn't say which count is the span, the vertical depth, or the width. In this paper y is the vertical/build axis (Fig. 2(a), Eq. 12). The top3d ordering (nelx×nely×nelz) puts 20 elements along y. But in Sec. 4.2 the refined case with the same boundary conditions is split 'evenly in the y-direction' into 4 batches of 5400 voxels. A proportional 60×30×12 grid can only be split that way along its 60- or 12-element axis, which weakly suggests y is not the 20-element axis.
readings: x = 40 (span), y = 20 (vertical depth), z = 8 (width), i.e. top3d ordering
x = 40 (span), y = 8 (vertical depth), z = 20 (width)

items.description: No physical lengths or element size are given for the 40×20×8 hexahedral grid. The FE code is ported from Liu & Tovar, which uses unit cubic H8 elements, but Sec. 3.4 normalizes coordinates so the longest edge runs from -0.5 to 0.5.
readings: unit cubic elements, so the domain is 40 × 20 × 8 units
cubic elements of edge 1/40, so the domain is 1 × 0.5 × 0.2

items.description: Sec. 4.1 only refers to 'the same cantilever beam boundary condition'. Where the fixed region is and how far it extends is shown only in Fig. 3(a), which isn't available. Liu & Tovar's default cantilever, the code this solver is based on, clamps the whole x = 0 face.
readings: entire end face x = 0 (all nodes on that face)
only the top and bottom edges (y = 0 and y = H) of the x = 0 face

items.description: Which displacement components are fixed at the support is not stated anywhere in the text; it is only in Fig. 3(a).
readings: fully clamped: ux = uy = uz = 0 at every support node (top3d default)
partially restrained: only the axial and load-direction components fixed, plus the minimum extra restraint needed to stop rigid-body motion

items.entity: Tip load location on the free end
items.description: The text does not describe where the load is applied (Fig. 3(a) only). For a cantilever it is presumably at the free end (x = L), but its height on the end face is unknown.
readings: bottom edge of the free end: x = L, y = 0 (top3d default)
mid-height of the free end: x = L, y = 0.5H
top edge of the free end: x = L, y = H

items.entity: Spatial distribution of the tip load
items.description: The text doesn't say whether the load is a line load across the width, a single nodal force, or a traction on the end face (Fig. 3(a) only).
readings: line load across the full width: equal forces on all nodes from z = 0 to W (9 nodes for an 8-element width; top3d default)
single point force at mid-width (z = 0.5W)
uniform traction over the whole free-end face

items.description: The direction is shown only in Fig. 3(a). It is presumably transverse to the span, but the text doesn't say whether it acts along the 20-element or the 8-element cross-section axis. The sign does not change compliance.
readings: along the 20-element axis (-y, strong-axis bending; top3d default)
along the 8-element axis (weak-axis bending)

items.description: No force value is given. top3d applies -1 at each loaded node. If the Fig. 4 beam has the same boundary conditions, its compliance (c = 20.9 at 40×20×16) is about half of Fig. 3's (c ≈ 40 at 40×20×8). That weakly suggests the total load is held fixed rather than the per-node load.
readings: unit force per loaded node (top3d default)
unit total force shared equally by the loaded nodes
another physical magnitude

items.description: V* appears only as a symbol in Eq. (20). No value is given for the validation case or anywhere else in the paper.
readings: 0.3 (Liu & Tovar default)

items.description: Eq. (6) uses E0, but no value is given (Sec. 3.2 says only that the material is isotropic).
readings: E0 = 1, normalized (top3d default)
physical modulus of the print material (e.g., about 2.5 GPa for a polymer or 200 GPa for steel)

items.description: Sec. 3.2 says the material is isotropic linear elastic but gives no Poisson's ratio.
readings: 0.3 (top3d default)

items.description: Eq. (6) includes Emin, but its value (or its ratio to E0) is not given.
readings: 1e-9·E0 (top3d default)

items.description: The exponent p in Eq. (6) is not given, and no continuation scheme is mentioned. It applies to both the NN run and the SIMP baseline.
readings: p = 3 fixed (top3d default)
continuation from p = 1 to 3

items.entity: Filter in the element-wise SIMP baseline (Fig. 3(c))
items.description: Sec. 4.1 says the NN avoids checkerboards 'without needing filtering'. It never says whether the SIMP baseline it is compared with used a density or sensitivity filter, or what radius. The Liu & Tovar code it builds on uses a density filter.
readings: no filter (raw element densities)
density filter, rmin = 1.5 elements (top3d default)
sensitivity filter, rmin = 1.5 elements

items.description: Sec. 3.1 uses Keras RandomFourierFeatures with kernels 'initialized in a linear 3D grid'. It does not give the number of features, the grid range or spacing, the kernel scale, or whether the kernels are trainable. These set the implicit length scale that replaces filtering in Fig. 3(b).
readings: one kernel per element on a 40×20×8 grid (6400 features)
coarser grid, e.g. 20×10×4 (800 features)
same grid with a different Gaussian scale (e.g., 1 vs 10), which changes the minimum member size

items.description: Sec. 4.1 and the Fig. 3 caption say SGD is used for iterations 1-100 and Adam for 101-300. Learning rates and momentum are not given, and it isn't explicit whether this schedule applies to the NN run, the SIMP baseline, or both.
readings: Keras defaults: SGD lr = 0.01 without momentum, then Adam lr = 0.001
larger steps: SGD lr = 0.1, then Adam lr = 0.01

items.description: Sec. 3.5 says α1 starts at 0 and is 'gradually' increased every iteration up to a cap of 100, but the increment is not given. Because the volume constraint is a penalty term, the final volume and the optimization path depend on it.
readings: linear ramp reaching 100 at iteration 300
+0.5 per iteration, reaching 100 at iteration 200
linear ramp reaching 100 by iteration 100, then held constant

items.entity: SIMP-baseline design variables and initial design
items.description: Sec. 4.1 builds the SIMP baseline as a one-layer net with a constant input and one output per element. It doesn't say how the outputs are kept within [0,1] (sigmoid or clipping) or what their initial values are; Sec. 3.5 says only that c0 is computed for a uniform V* design.
readings: per-element variables initialized to V* and clipped to [0,1]
sigmoid-mapped variables initialized at logit(V*), giving a uniform V* start
sigmoid with zero weights, giving a uniform 0.5 start
